chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn and ʿAlī ibn al-Sindī, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū Ibrāhīm عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about the junub and the menstruating woman touching silver coins with their hands. He said: There is no harm.

So this does not contradict the first report, because it is possible that he only permitted that for him when the name of Allah, Exalted is He, was not on them, even if they were silver; and in the first report there is a prohibition from touching them when there is something of that upon them.

key_terms.اسْمُ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى: the name of Allah, Exalted is He
key_terms.الْجُنُبِ: a person in a state of janabah requiring ghusl
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or objection

ai.seo_question: Can a junub person or a menstruating woman touch coins that bear the name of Allah?
ai.summary: This hadith indicates that a junub person or a menstruating woman may touch silver coins, and there is no harm in doing so. The accompanying explanation reconciles this with an earlier report by stating that the permission applies when the coins do not bear the name of Allah, Exalted is He, whereas prohibition applies when they do.
